items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-27
items.q: I used Johnny when I had charge of the Studebaker transcriptions.

ctx.x: That's where we were... Down there... On Bourbon Street... And, uh... He was responsible... He and Johnny Detroit... Well... There were... Two musicians... Who were more businessmen... Than the average musician... Because musicians are not... Not... Musicians are not businessmen... Uh-huh... In fact, my father had the opportunity... After we... After we bought that place down there... At a stupid price... Sam Burglass... On Burglass Furniture Store... On Canal Street... He was the... Exalted ruler... Of the...…

items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-20
items.q: Johnny Detroit had a great respect for him [my father]... he played for him... he asked my daddy to substitute for him

ctx.x: But your dad was the only one that played, huh?

My, uh, father was the only one that played. He played the Cronolet, and, uh, he played pretty, pretty good. In fact, Johnny Detroit had a great respect for him, a great admiration for him, and he played for him. I mean, uh, great admiration for him. Yeah. Uh, when Johnny went to New York, he was working on the fountain grill of the Rosefeld Hotel, and he asked my daddy to substitute for him playing his place, and he did for about six weeks, I think it was. And he was very elated the way my father played. He…
Well, where was this that he substituted for?
